nodes.name: Phytoplankton
nodes.desc: Microscopic drifting algae, including diatoms, that capture sunlight in the bay and fjord waters and feed the marine food chain.

nodes.name: Green alder
nodes.desc: A shrub that colonises ground left bare by retreating ice. Alders host nitrogen-fixing root bacteria that enrich young soils.

nodes.name: Willows
nodes.desc: Several willow species grow on new ground and river flats near the bay. Moose and voles use them for food.

nodes.name: Sitka spruce
nodes.desc: A large conifer that forms the forest of the lower bay, on ground exposed by ice long ago.

nodes.name: Krill
nodes.desc: Small shrimp-like crustaceans that graze plankton and swarm in coastal water. A main food for humpbacks and schooling fish.

nodes.name: Pacific herring
nodes.desc: A schooling fish that feeds on plankton and is eaten by whales, seals, birds and salmon-eating predators.

nodes.name: Blue mussels
nodes.desc: Shellfish of rocky shores that filter plankton from the water. Sea otters crack them open.

nodes.name: Moose
nodes.desc: A large browser of willows and other shrubs on river flats and young forest. Wolves and brown bears can take them.

nodes.name: Long-tailed vole
nodes.desc: A small plant-eating rodent of meadows and shrubby ground, recorded often in the area. Food for bears and other predators.

nodes.name: Pacific salmon
nodes.desc: Salmon feed at sea, then return to streams to spawn and die. Their bodies carry ocean energy to bears, eagles, wolves and scavengers.

nodes.name: Humpback whale
nodes.desc: The most recorded mammal near the park. It feeds on krill and small schooling fish in the bay in summer.

nodes.name: Sea otter
nodes.desc: A marine weasel that eats shellfish and other seafloor animals. It is recorded in the park and is preyed on by orcas.

nodes.name: Harbor seal
nodes.desc: Eats fish such as herring and salmon, and rests on ice and shore. Orcas hunt them.

nodes.name: Bald eagle
nodes.desc: One of the most recorded birds here. It takes fish such as salmon and herring and scavenges carcasses.

nodes.name: Common raven
nodes.desc: An opportunistic bird that scavenges carcasses of salmon and large animals.

nodes.name: Orca
nodes.desc: A top marine predator. Mammal-eating orcas hunt seals, porpoises, sea otters and sometimes whales.

nodes.name: Brown bear
nodes.desc: An omnivore that eats salmon, small mammals, moose and plants. Salmon carried inland add marine nutrients to the land.

nodes.name: Gray wolf
nodes.desc: A pack hunter of the park's forests. It hunts moose and also eats salmon.

nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Long summer days power plankton blooms in the bay and plant growth on the land.

nodes.name: Retreating glaciers
nodes.desc: Glaciers have been receding for decades, leaving bare ground where plants then colonise in stages.

nodes.name: Glacial meltwater
nodes.desc: Cold, silty meltwater flows into the fjords and mixes with sea water, affecting where plankton grows.

nodes.name: Young soils
nodes.desc: Thin soils left behind by ice build up as plants grow and die and as nitrogen is added.

nodes.name: Decomposers
nodes.desc: Fungi, bacteria and invertebrates that break down dead plants, fish and carcasses and return nutrients to the soil.
